title: TypeScript SDK: robust AsyncIterable <-> Web Streams interop with backpressure & resumable retries
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Goal:
Deliver a developer-friendly TypeScript SDK streaming API that interoperates seamlessly between AsyncIterable and WHATWG ReadableStream in both Node and browser environments, supports backpressure semantics, and enables resumable retries for transient network failures.

Problem statement:
Current SDK provides streaming helpers but has gaps: users struggle when mixing async iterators and Web Streams (pipeTo / pipeThrough), backpressure is inconsistent between Node vs browser, and retries either drop partial progress or double-consume buffers leading to memory spikes. We need a single user ergonomics pattern plus compatibility layer and examples.

Design proposals (summary):
1) Primary public surface: `client.stream(...)` returns a StreamingResponse object with two ergonomic accessors: `asyncIterator()` and `webStream()` (lazy created). This avoids forcing one primitive.
2) Backpressure model: Implement a continuous-pull consumer inside the runtime that honors WHATWG backpressure by reading only when consumer requests next chunk. For Node-only environments, map to native stream backpressure semantics using TransformStream polyfill when necessary.
3) Retry strategy: For idempotent generation calls, support resumable retries by checkpointing output byte offsets + model cache keys. On retry, the server-side resume token is requested and SDK will rehydrate the KV cache and continue reading. If resumability not supported, provide an opt-in memory buffered fallback with a configurable maxBufferBytes.
4) Interop utilities: Provide `fromAsyncIteratorToWebStream(iterator)` and `fromWebStreamToAsyncIterator(stream)` helpers that preserve backpressure and correctly close on upstream error/cancel. These helpers should be small (<= 120 LOC) and well-tested.

Trade-offs considered:
- Memory vs latency: buffering for resume simplifies retries but increases memory. We choose a conservative default (no buffering) and surface `maxBufferBytes` for users requiring it.
- Complexity: exposing two accessors increases API surface but keeps ergonomic defaults.
- Polyfills: shipping a lightweight TransformStream shim for older Node versions increases bundle size (~1.8KB minified) but improves DX. We'll gate inclusion behind bundler tree-shaking and point to CDN alternative.

Acceptance criteria:
- New StreamingResponse with asyncIterator() and webStream() documented and tested.
- Interop helpers added with unit tests covering cancel/error/backpressure semantics.
- Retry flow validated end-to-end with a stubbed server that returns resume tokens.
- Example apps: Node (fastify) and Browser (React) demos showing piping to <textarea> and to WritableStream.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for helpers simulating slow consumer and fast producer (backpressure preserved).
- Integration tests using Playwright for browser example and Node harness for native streams.
- Load benchmark: compare memory/latency vs current implementation with 100 concurrent streams of 2KB/sec token emission.

Artifacts / references:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/TS+Streaming+Interoperability (draft)
- Spike PR with prototype helpers: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1842 (WIP)
- Example app branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/compare/streaming-interop

Open questions / TODOs:
- Server handshake for resume tokens: do we require model-side support before enabling resume by default? (short-term: opt-in via `resumable: true`)
- Telemetry: what metrics for partial-consume vs cancel should be emitted? (add ticket to instrumentation backlog)

Progress updates (chronological):
- 2026-03-12: Kickoff. Spike demo showed feasible mapping of AsyncIterator -> TransformStream in Node. Linked prototype PR.
- 2026-03-13: UX review with PM/Docs: agreed on `StreamingResponse{ asyncIterator(), webStream() }` shape. Docs owner: Mei Park.
- 2026-03-14: Engineering review: decided to avoid automatic buffering; add `maxBufferBytes` option and explicit `resumable` flag. Prototype PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1842/files

Implementation plan (next steps):
1) Finalize helper APIs and add type definitions (this ticket).
2) Implement core runtime adapter that creates TransformStreams on demand, respecting backpressure.
3) Wire resumable retry hooks and add unit/integration tests.
4) Docs + sample apps + migration notes.

Notes for reviewers:
- Look for correctness in cancellation semantics: upstream cancellation should propagate to both asyncIterator and webStream accessors and must free internal buffers.
- Pay attention to Node 18 vs Node 20 streams behavior — include targeted tests for both.
steps: 1) Merge prototype helpers PR (review comments resolved). 2) Implement runtime adapter and add TransformStream polyfill where necessary. 3) Add resume token handshake and optional buffering. 4) Add tests and Playwright example. 5) Publish docs and release in sdk-2026.03
